name: Red Gates (Aktash)
full: A narrow gorge with red cliffs in the Chibitka river valley on the Aktash — Ulagan — Balyktuyul road (Ulagan Trakt), ~8 km from the village of Aktash, at the junction of the Kurai and Aygulak ranges.
near: Aktash village (~8 km, welcometoaltai; altertravel gives 15 km — a discrepancy); Ulagan village is ~33 km further along the road (estimate: the whole Aktash — Ulagan road is ~41 km, TASS).
elev: not found (Aktash ~1400 m; the exact elevation of the gorge is not confirmed)
short: A natural monument: the road to Ulagan squeezes between sheer red-pink cliffs ~50 m high, coloured by cinnabar (mercury ore); a short but striking stop on the way to Ulagan Pass and Katu-Yaryk Pass.
desc: The Red Gates are a narrow, winding passage between sheer cliffs about 50 m high in the Chibitka river valley, where the Ulagan Trakt (Aktash — Ulagan — Balyktuyul) crosses the Kurai and Aygulak ranges. The cliffs are made of effusive (volcanic) rocks, and their pink-red colour comes from mercury compounds — cinnabar; near Aktash there is the Aktash mercury deposit (discovered in 1935, the plant started up in December 1942 — visit-altairepublic.ru), with the mine in the highlands at ~50.19, 87.43. The passage was originally almost impassable; the road was blasted through and a bridge was thrown across the Chibitka; an inscription dated 1945/1946 survives on the right-hand cliff (2GIS mentions inscriptions by soldiers from May 1945, welcometoaltai says 1946), and it is regularly touched up. The site is a natural monument of the Altai Republic. A decision on a bypass was made after public discussions: in 2020 (TASS, gorno-altaisk.info 07.09.2020), during repairs of the Aktash — Ulagan road, they planned to build an alternative route at km 8 so as not to blast the cliffs, and to eventually turn the old road through the gates into a pedestrian tourist route; as of 2024, 64 of the 71.7 km of the Ulagan Trakt had been repaired and paved (gorno-altaisk.info, 12.2024) — whether the bypass has been built is not confirmed. Further along the road are the Dead Lake (Cheybekkol), Lake Uzunkol, Ulagan Pass (2080 m), the Pazyryk burial mounds and Katu-Yaryk Pass into the Chulyshman valley.
guide: Don't stop right in the narrows, but a little before or after them — that way you'll see how the cliffs “close” over the road. The red colour is cinnabar, mercury ore: don't lick the rocks or take them with you, even though they are harmless to the touch. Look for the old post-war inscription on the right-hand cliff — it has been touched up for almost 80 years. In the sun the cliffs glow scarlet, and on an overcast evening they turn gloomy — locals say the gates “let you in” to the Ulagan region. From here it is 4 km to the Dead Lake, Cheybekkol — stop by, it's on the way.
see: The narrows between the red cliffs and the bridge over the Chibitka; the 1945/46 inscription on the right-hand cliff; the Dead Lake, Cheybekkol (~4 km further, welcometoaltai); Lake Uzunkol; Ulagan Pass (2080 m) with a gazebo and viewing platform (Tolk 2026); waterfalls on the Boka river (~19 km, altertravel); the Kurai steppe (~23 km).
skip: If you aren't going to Ulagan/Chulyshman, a 16 km round-trip detour from Aktash just for 5–10 minutes at the cliffs is only worth it for photographers.
diff: Very easy — a viewing stop by the road.
when: June — September (dry road, Chulyshman season); passable in winter, but there is icing on the Ulagan Trakt (Tolk 08.2025).
hours: Open 24 hours, free (a natural monument by the highway).
daytime: A sunny day, midday — the cliffs are bright red (turistka, 2GIS); in the evening in overcast weather — a gloomy atmosphere.
how: Take the Chuysky Trakt to the village of Aktash (km 788), at the junction at km ~790.7 turn toward Ulagan (Ulagan Trakt), ~8 km along the Chibitka valley to the gates. Biysk to the gates ~463 km (welcometoaltai). The Aktash — Ulagan road has been repaired and paved for most of its length (64 of 71.7 km by 12.2024; another 7.7 km under the national project in 2025).
needcar: Yes — a car/taxi from Aktash; on foot it is ~8 km along the road from Aktash.
self: Yes, easy — no permits needed (Ulagan district is outside the border zone).
roadtype: Paved road (the Ulagan Trakt was repaired in 2022–2024, gorno-altaisk.info); some repair sections at km 29 (2025, temporary detour — Tolk 08.08.2025).
traveltime: Aktash — gates ~10–15 min; Gorno-Altaysk — Aktash ~5 h by marshrutka (minibus) (avtovokzaly); Biysk — gates ~463 km, 7–8 h by car (estimate).
stay: Aktash: the Krasnye Vorota (Red Gates) base (Leninskaya St. 63a, +7 961 893-52-42, kvorota.ru, from 6200 ₽ (RUB), 2GIS 4.9/106); Gorny Orel, Kak Doma (101hotels, 9.6/10); Aktash has 20+ hotels from ~4600 ₽ (RUB) (101hotels 2026); guesthouses 6–9 km from the gates from 200 ₽ (RUB) (welcometoaltai, outdated).
net: There is a signal in Aktash (a repeater); in the narrows — not found, check.
entry: Free (a natural monument by the road; no information about a fee found).
bring: A camera (wide-angle lens), a jacket — it's windy; if you're continuing on to Chulyshman — a full tank in Aktash/at the junction (fuel station at km 790.7).
warn: Stopping in the narrow gorge on the roadway is dangerous — park in the wider spots before/after. Rockfalls from the cliffs are possible. In winter — icing on the Ulagan Trakt. Do not chip off cinnabar (mercury ore; the Aktash mercury mine is an environmentally problematic area). Ticks (season May–July).
food: In Aktash (2GIS, 2026): Oasis (4.8, 935 ratings, home cooking), Karavan (4.4, 486, check ~400 ₽ (RUB)), M52 (4.5, 242, ~500 ₽ (RUB)), Myaso Khleb (4.9, 139, ~650 ₽ (RUB)), Teertpek (4.8, 232, Altai cuisine and game, ~1200 ₽ (RUB)).
reviews: 2GIS: 4.8 out of 5 (68 ratings, 50 reviews, 202 photos) — 2026; TripAdvisor: 4.3/5 (27 reviews), No. 3 of 5 in Aktash. Pros: bright colour, unusual, on the way; cons: a short stop, narrow road, nowhere to pull over.
p.sum: The Red Gates are 8 km from Aktash on the paved Ulagan Trakt; a free 10–20 minute stop on the way to Ulagan Pass, Pazyryk and Katu-Yaryk Pass. Lodging and food are in Aktash.
